rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline is informative and how strong the validation signal is before adding complexity. config_001 tests the minimal RNA single-profile PCA setup with no aggregation or fusion, providing a clean reference for later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion. It is the best first use of budget because it is simple, interpretable, and reduces uncertainty about the baseline contribution of RNA representation.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline, so the largest uncertainty is whether image data provides useful predictive signal. config_010 tests a minimal image-only ResNet-50 single-profile baseline, isolating the value of the image modality before adding fusion, multiprofile, or stronger encoders. This is the best use of the next limited experiment because it creates an image baseline needed to compare modalities and to decide whether multimodal configurations are worth testing.

The only moderately strong result so far is config_001, RNA-only with PCA_n2000 and singleprofile, with validation accuracy 0.4849 and F1 0.4639, while image-only ResNet50 is much weaker at 0.2079. The key uncertainty is whether the RNA-only result can be improved by using multiprofile aggregation without changing the RNA representation. config_002 keeps the same RNA-only model setting and PCA_n2000 encoder as config_001 but tests multiprofile with avgpool, making it a direct, low-risk comparison that isolates the effect of profile/aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising current direction while avoiding confounding changes to RNA encoder, image modality, or fusion, and it will clarify whether multiprofile aggregation is worth further exploration before testing transformer aggregation or more complex multimodal models.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool (config_002) substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA (config_001), while image-only ResNet is weak. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for multiprofile RNA. config_003 changes only aggregation from config_002, isolating this effect and directly extending the current best direction. This is a high-value next step because it may raise validation accuracy and clarifies which aggregation to use before testing more complex multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the strongest result so far (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), while transformer aggregation and single-profile RNA are weaker, and image-only ResNet is poor. This tests whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improves over PCA under the same multiprofile avgpool setting, isolating the effect of RNA representation. It is a one-factor extension of the current best direction, making it more informative than jumping to multimodal or changing multiple settings.

RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is the strongest direction, with scvi_n200 achieving the best accuracy/F1 (0.650/0.628) and outperforming pca-based multiprofile models. The main uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation, which was worse than avgpool for pca, can improve or match scvi_n200 in the best profile setting. config_006 changes only aggregation from the current best RNA-only configuration, directly testing this encoder-aggregation interaction and helping decide whether to exploit avgpool or transformer before adding multimodal complexity.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only scvi_n200 multiprofile is the strongest direction, with config_005 and config_006 reaching about 0.65 validation accuracy and F1, while multiprofile also helped pca_n2000 and image-only resnet50 is weak. The key uncertainty is whether scvi_n200's strong performance is driven by the encoder alone or by multiprofile aggregation. config_004 tests scvi_n200 with singleprofile and no aggregation, directly isolating the profile-setting effect for the best RNA representation. This is a simple, high-potential ablation that avoids adding fusion or a second modality, and it clarifies whether the more complex multiprofile pipeline is necessary before spending budget on multimodal extensions.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models are strongest, with scvi_n200 + avgpool reaching 0.650 accuracy and transformer nearly matching it, while image-only ResNet50 is weak. The main uncertainty is whether the RNA encoder choice (scvi vs scgpt) materially affects performance under the best-known multiprofile/avgpool setting. config_008 tests scgpt with the same multiprofile + avgpool design as config_005, isolating the RNA encoder effect. This is the best next use of budget because it extends the most promising direction with a single controlled change, can identify a better RNA representation, and avoids prematurely adding multimodal complexity while image evidence remains weak.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only scvi with multiprofile is much better than PCA or scgpt, and transformer aggregation gives a small but consistent edge over avgpool (0.653 vs 0.650 accuracy). Image-only ResNet is weak, so it is unclear whether image features add complementary value to a strong RNA model. config_032 extends the best RNA setting with ResNet image and simple concat fusion, directly comparing against the RNA-only transformer baseline to isolate the effect of adding image. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising RNA configuration while testing the central multimodal question with minimal added complexity.

RNA-only scvi multiprofile models are strong (0.650-0.653 accuracy), image-only single ResNet50 is weak (0.208 accuracy), and the only multimodal result so far is best but sparse and confounds adding image, fusion, and complexity. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality contributes at all when given multiprofile aggregation. config_012 tests image-only ResNet50 with multiprofile transformer aggregation, holding image encoder and aggregation fixed relative to the best multimodal config while removing RNA/fusion. This is the best next experiment because it is a simpler baseline that reduces uncertainty about an important design choice before further multimodal exploitation: if image-only is weak, the multimodal gain likely depends on fusion/interaction, while if it is strong, image representation becomes a clear axis for future encoder or fusion tests.
